newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.N. chief starts first African tour.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief starts first African tour.

text.p: U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan began his first official visit to Africa on Wednesday, promising to participate personally in the attempts to broker peace in Zaire and to help put Angola's peace process on track.

Annan arrived in Cape Town on a scheduled flight from the United States and is due to meet President Nelson Mandela, who recently launched a personal initiative to bring Zaire's warring sides together.

In remarks on his arrival in South Africa, Annan said he hoped an African leaders' summit, which began in Nairobi on Wednesday, could decide the future of the peace process. The rebels, who were not invited, have dismissed the meeting as useless.
He added that he would personally attend a further summit in Lome, Togo on March 26.
"I expect to join heads of state in Lome to assist in the search for peace in Zaire," he said.
He said both Zaire's government and rebels led by Laurent Kabila had accepted a five-point peace plan with reservations, but added that he expected the plan to form the basis of a settlement.
Annan, a native of Ghana, said he was told when he boarded the aircraft in Miami that a hitch had arisen in the formation next week of an Angolan government of national unity.

The U.N. chief said he would go to Angola after South Africa to see for himself progress in a two-year-old peace between the government and former rebel UNITA who fought a bloody 19-year civil war until a 1994 peace agreement.
Angola hosts the U.N.'s largest peacekeeping mission of around 7,000 members.

"I hope it will be possible that a national unity government will be formed during my visit to Angola. The people of Angola deserve it, they are tired of war and their leaders have to have the courage to give them peace," he said.
